title: Number of Connected Island Landmasses
statement_md:
Given an `m x n` 2D binary grid `grid` which represents a map of `'1'`s (land) and `'0'`s (water), return the number of islands.

An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically. You may assume all four edges of the grid are all surrounded by water.

### Input Format
- A JSON-encoded 2D list of strings `grid`

### Output Format
- An integer representing island count

hints.text: Scan every cell of the grid. Whenever you find '1', increment island count and sink the island.
Sinking the island means setting all 4-directionally connected '1's to '0' via traversal.
Use Depth-First Search (DFS) or Breadth-First Search (BFS) to flood all connected land cells.

editorial_md:
### Optimal Approach: Connected Components DFS

Iterate over every cell `(r, c)`. If `grid[r][c] == '1'`, increment `count` and trigger DFS to mark all connected land cells as `'0'`.

#### Complexity
- **Time Complexity:** $O(m \cdot n)$ each cell visited at most constant times.
- **Space Complexity:** $O(m \cdot n)$ recursion call stack.

#### Common Pitfalls
- Diagonals do NOT connect land cells.
